title: Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
content_md: Adobe, Veeam, and Juniper Networks have released patches for over three dozen vulnerabilities across their products, including multiple critical-severity code execution flaws. This week, Adobe fixed 12 vulnerabilities in Campaign Classic, Connect, Creative Cloud, and Substance 3D Painter. The Campaign Classic update resolves eight critical-severity bugs, including code/command injection, incorrect authorization, and XSS issues. Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation, Adobe warns in a priority 2 advisory. Another critical-severity defect leading to arbitrary code execution was addressed in Adobe Connect for desktop and mobile. The security updates for Creative Cloud and Substance 3D Painter resolve high- and medium-severity security holes leading to code execution, privilege escalation, and memory leaks. Adobe says it is not aware of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild. Veeam rolled out fixes for nine security defects in Backup for Microsoft 365, Backup & Replication, Veeam ONE, and Veeam Agent for Linux. In Backup for Microsoft 365, Veeam fixed four flaws, including a critical issue that could have allowed attackers to read/write configuration data cross-tenant and achieve remote code execution.
